investigation.summary: Discount logic uses strict greater-than instead of greater-or-equal, causing exact thresholds ($100, $250) to skip intended tiers.

limitations: Only tested discount logic; did not isolate roundCents behavior or tax module interactions directly.

verdictHistory.note: 3 competing hypotheses; no experiment has run yet.

Observed — reproduction 1/1 failed; repeated runs 10/10 failed; parent commit 0/3 failed. Evidence rubric: moderate. "Confirmed" requires strong experimental evidence; the evidence rubric rates it moderate.

hypotheses.cause: Operator regression: `>=` changed to `>` in tier qualification, causing exact threshold amounts to fall through to the default rate 0.
hypotheses.assessment: Deterministic failure reproduced at current commit; parent commit passes same test; failure persists across retries.

hypotheses.cause: New `roundCents` function silently truncates the discount calculation, producing incorrect rates for edge-case subtotals.
hypotheses.assessment: No experiment tested H2; but given H1 explains all observations precisely, H2 is unnecessary.

hypotheses.cause: Tax.js `Object.freeze` and `hasOwnProperty` change introduced a module loading side-effect that corrupts the discounts module scope.

hypotheses.assessment: External search yielded no actionable evidence; no experiment isolated tax-module side effects.

patches.title: Targeted fix by Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b
patches.rationale: The root cause is the operator regression in discountRate: the condition changed from `>=` to `>` in the tier qualification logic. This causes exact threshold amounts (10000, 25000, 50000 cents) to fall through to the default rate 0. The fix is to change the comparison back to `>=` so that orders meeting the exact threshold qualify for the tier.
